name: 2015 livery
description: Red nose back past the cockpit, its aft edge curving from the crown down to the nose gear; white cabin with a big indigo lower-case 'edelweiss' and 'Switzerland' small beneath. Red sweeps up from the rear fuselage into an all-red fin carrying a huge white edelweiss flower with a yellow center. White tail cone and engines, red wingtips.

sources.note: ICAO EDW; the revised livery first applied in November 2015, then fleet-wide.

areas.name: red nose, aft edge curving from the crown (far back) down and forward to the belly
red rear fuselage under the fin, from a point on the crown sweeping down aft

logos.description: An edelweiss flower: a star of long white pointed petals (about ten) round a yellow center of seven round florets; big enough to spill past the fin's trailing edge near the root.

titles.style: Heavy lower-case rounded sans, wide, upright, crossing the window line from just behind the red nose to over the wing.
Small regular sans, mixed case, under the start of 'edelweiss'.

notes: Not drawn: registration with Swiss flag and 'Member of Lufthansa Group' aft. The A340 and A350 carry the same design scaled to the type. The flower's petals reach slightly onto the fuselage at the fin's trailing-edge root. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on HB-JJK (left, level, 2026-10-07), measured between its doors on the A320 shape and by the window line: edelweiss runs x 0.223-0.567 (it had started at 0.194), its baseline at the windows' foot and its ascenders 0.76 high (lowercase 0.79 of them); Switzerland under its start (0.224-0.274). Both red fields' edges are curves (smooth). The left photo puts the nose red's top on the crown ~1.3 m further aft (x ~0.29) than drawn, but the right-side photo (from above) shows the edge nearly upright: left as drawn.
history: New in the dataset (Skyarium v1 had no Edelweiss entry). The 2015 livery replaced the earlier white scheme with the flower on a red fin and red script titles.
